unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 9 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.1 - THEME 7: LIFE IN NATURE & GLOBAL PROBLEMS

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will search for the theme ''Life in Nature and Global Problems'' by examining the effects of humans on natural disasters and effects of natural disasters on nature and humans and the role of technology in addressing global issues such as healthcare, AI, and data solutions. Students will research a specific natural disaster for the details of its environmental and human impact and suggest innovative solutions for being prepared for disasters or recovery by using modern technology. They will design a multimedia presentation or poster showing how technological developments such as AI for disaster prediction can lessen the effects of these disasters. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in nature and global problems with its components such as natural disasters and their impact on nature; natural disasters and their impact on humans; impact of technology on global issues (AI, data, healthcare)'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school may know what natural disasters and their impact on nature; natural disasters and their impact on humans; impact of technology on global issues (AI, data, healthcare) mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in nature and global problems'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''life in nature and global problems with its components such as natural disasters and their impact on nature; natural disasters and their impact on humans; impact of technology on global issues (AI, data, healthcare)'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the poster and/ or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about natural disasters and their influence on nature; natural disasters and their influence on humans in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Disaster Response Simulation Students work in small groups, and the teacher assigns each group a disaster scenario (e.g. a flood destroying a village, a volcanic eruption threatening a town). Within each group, students take roles such as ''Emergency Responder, Local Authority, Environmental Scientist, and Survivor''. They role-play a meeting to discuss the disaster’s effects by using target vocabulary (e.g. rescue, destruction, survival) and target grammar (e.g. ''The flood, which destroyed our homes, left us desperate for help''). After their discussions, groups present a summary to the class, and the teacher gives feedback on use of vocabulary, grammar, and also of communication. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To talk about natural disasters and their impact on nature in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Match and design Students work in small groups, and the teacher provides each group with two sets of cards: one with target vocabulary (e.g. earthquake, habitat, harm) and another with their definitions. Groups match the words with the correct definitions. After matching, each group selects 3-4 words and makes sentences by using them, encouraging the use of relative clauses (which, who, that) when possible. For example: ''The earthquake that struck the city caused great damage''. Groups share their sentences with the class, and the teacher gives feedback on the use of grammar and vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
